classification_decisions.case: binding display-gate coupling (the structural survivor family)
classification_decisions.reproduction: On the released v0.3.0, direct construction of the EXPORTED BindingResult type -- BindingResult(run_id='x', checks={'B1': False}) -- yielded status PROVEN: the old status derived FAILED only from the findings list and ignored a False check value. A 256-combination constructive probe over the check_binding pipeline found no input producing this state end-to-end.
classification_decisions.position_for_a_number: BindingResult is exported at package top level and listed in __all__; the contradictory state was reproducible on the unchanged release artifact, and the fix changed observable public behaviour -- released behaviour under the numbering rule.
classification_decisions.position_against: BindingResult is an OUTPUT type: check_binding produces it, consumers read it. Hand-constructing one with contradictory fields is not an input to the system but fabrication of a result object. No supported usage path produced a wrong verdict; the defect is that the type permitted representing an invalid state -- a design weakness (make invalid states unrepresentable), not observed misbehaviour. Numbering output-type invariant gaps would dilute the ledger: any dataclass that does not validate itself would qualify.
classification_decisions.rule_refined: A finding number marks released behaviour reachable through a SUPPORTED USAGE PATH. Output-type invariant gaps get the canonicalisation fix, tests, and a non-silent register entry -- this one.
classification_decisions.scope_note: The earlier 'the 256-case probe closes this' judgement claimed more than the probe covered: the probe spanned the check_binding pipeline, the judgement spoke of the released code entire. A closing judgement must not outrange the probe it cites.
classification_decisions.output_type_sweep: DispatchScore (counters vs detail) and Outcome (overall vs reasons) carry the same dual-representation pattern; exit_code is derived and cannot disagree. Resolution: documented producer guarantee in their docstrings rather than canonicalisation, because deriving DispatchScore's counters from detail would change the serialised shape earlier deposited artifacts already carry. Neither silent, nor numbered.
classification_decisions.measured_fact: Wheel probe on the released v0.3.0 (installed from the checksum-matched GitHub release): checks={'B1': None} -> UNPROVEN with an empty explanatory list; checks={'B1': False} -> PROVEN. Correctly scoped, this refines the DESCRIPTION, not the reachability: the None branch is PRODUCER-REACHABLE and correctly handled -- check_binding writes None for an unprovable B3 and the status honours it -- while False on the supported path always co-arrived with a finding, so the status was correct there too. The erroneous combination (False with an empty findings list) arises only through unsupported direct construction.
classification_decisions.decision_basis: Settled by the RULE, not by the strength of the arguments: a finding number marks released behaviour reachable through a supported usage path, and reachability is a question of fact. The alternative rule keyed on whether the field already defined semantics would reopen interpretation at every edge case.
classification_decisions.decision_history: This classification turned four times (no number -> #31 -> no number -> #31 -> no number final) across three review rounds and two measured probes -- more than the fix itself cost. The full #31 text is preserved in position_for_a_number; the case is closed and does not reopen without supported-path-reproducible evidence.
